players.product: infrared and visible optical components, Black Diamond infrared glass (used instead of germanium), assemblies and modules, and infrared cameras

quarterly_data.signal: LightPath's 10-Q for fiscal Q3 2026 (quarter ended March 31, 2026): revenue $19,149,814 versus $9,167,627 a year earlier (+109%), and $50,559,747 for the first nine months (+102%); gross profit $6,956,283; net loss $4,106,287; adjusted EBITDA $1,137,167 (6% of revenue). Assemblies and modules revenue rose $6.6 million, or 355%, of which approximately $6.4 million came from higher G5 Infrared camera and module sales, including the previously announced program with a large global technology customer; management expects continued growth in this product group based on backlog. Revenue by region for the quarter: United States $10,121,552, Europe $6,978,833 (versus $2,267,780), China $1,036,800.

LightPath's 10-Q backlog disclosure: total backlog was approximately $110.6 million at March 31, 2026, up 196% from $37.4 million at June 30, 2025 (quarter-end backlog $86,043 thousand in Q1 2026, $97,837 thousand in Q2 2026 and $110,557 thousand in Q3 2026). G5 Infrared backlog was $80.6 million versus $16.6 million at June 30, 2025; the increase includes approximately $58.0 million in orders from a leading global technology customer (not named) for advanced infrared camera systems expected to ship in calendar years 2026 and 2027, plus several other multi-million dollar orders. LightPath orders added approximately $8.1 million, primarily infrared components; the AML acquisition added $1.1 million; and the company received a significant contract renewal for advanced infrared optics for a critical international military program. Nine-month working capital investment of $2.7 million was largely supplier prepayments for critical materials with long lead times.
